group_name: Carbon Steel / Alloy Steel / Free-cutting Steel
machining_characteristics: Generates long, continuous chips. Moderate cutting temperatures. BUE risk at low cutting speeds — use positive rake and good chip control.
Work-hardens rapidly. Low thermal conductivity traps heat at the edge. Use sharp positive geometry, consistent feed, and avoid dwelling.

typical_materials: Gray CI (G3000), Ductile CI (65-45-12), CGI, white CI, malleable CI
machining_characteristics: Short, brittle chips — abrasive on cutting edge. Low cutting forces but high tool wear. Run dry whenever possible.

typical_materials: Aluminum alloys (6061, 7075), Copper, Brass, Bronze, Mg alloys, CFRP, plastics
machining_characteristics: Low cutting forces and temperatures. High risk of BUE (built-up edge) on aluminum — use polished positive geometry and high cutting speeds.

typical_materials: Inconel 718, Inconel 625, Waspaloy, Hastelloy, Ti-6Al-4V, Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo
machining_characteristics: Extremely low thermal conductivity — heat concentrates at cutting edge. Run lower SFM, higher feed, with abundant high-pressure coolant.

group_name: Hardened Steel / Hardened Cast Iron / Chilled Cast Iron
typical_materials: Hardened tool steel, die steel, bearing races, rolls, HSS
machining_characteristics: Extreme hardness — standard carbide not suitable. Requires CBN, ceramic, or specialized PVD-coated micro-grain carbide; use rigid setups.
